newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares close down on Tenaga, Telekom sell-off.
newsitem.headline: KL shares close down on Tenaga, Telekom sell-off.

text.p: Malaysian blue-chip shares closed sharply lower on Tuesday after institutional investors sold down Tenaga, Telekom and Maybank stocks, said analysts.
The Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks was down 10.46 points or 0.84 percent to 1,228.89, and the small-capitalised Second Board index was down 11.26 to 622.42.

"Investors are taking profits on Tenaga and Telekom. Tenaga is being hit because the government said it is allowing a private power utility to set up, and Telekom because equal access is being brought forward," said Ooi Soon Beng, head of research at Inter-Pacific Securities.
"Tenaga and Telekom have contributed to a large part of the decline," said Patrick Tan, senior analyst at equities research house H.G. Asia in Kuala Lumpur.
Maybank was also subjected to profit taking after a recent rise on the back of expectations of strong interim results last Saturday. The stock was down 75 cents to 28.25 ringgit.
"At these levels it is fairly valued, and there has been some profit taking," said an analyst at a foreign brokerage house in Kuala Lumpur.
Total volume was 430 milion shares valued at 2.4 billion ringgit. Losers thumped gainers 353 to 262.
